_comment: #318 'THE NAME AND THE HABIT', the TALK route, end to end. Opens on the Lady's hub with I1 already closed, so the new entry row is the ONLY new row rendered there and every shipped I1 pin is provably untouched. Then the boulevard carriage wake (the felt-not-seen beat), the scribe's free refusal FOLLOWED by his [Charming Smile] chain, the broker's persuade chain, and the steward's report. OWNS THREE NEGATIVE PINS its siblings structurally cannot: the fixture holds [Charming Smile] and NOT [Appraise Foe] or [Stealth], and 25 gold against a 30-gold buy, so the scribe's blotter arm, the broker's lift arm and the broker's buy arm all render VISIBLE-LOCKED here with their exact requirement strings. FIX ROUND 1 added the run's FIRST leg -- the scribe BEFORE the card -- because his conversation is attached unconditionally (no `conversation_when` in the engine) and its quest gate therefore lives on the options; that leg is the only pin in the suite that proves the three banking arms are HIDDEN to a player who has not been shown the card. It also re-banks the SOCIAL route onto its own counter: the persuade fork banks block_handed_over, never block_bought_back, so the journal's history line and the steward's report row stop describing a 30-gold purchase this run provably never makes (gold is 25 at the broker and 25 after him). Seed inert -- no fight.

steps._comment: Title's default row is New Game -- down 1 to Continue, which loads the fixture-seeded manual slot.

== THE PRE-QUEST SCRIBE (FIX ROUND 1, the #318 gating pin). His `conversation` is attached with no gate -- the engine has no `conversation_when` -- so this graph is reachable the moment a player walks into the shop, and it opened two beats of the thread to someone who had never met the Lady. The gate now rides the OPTIONS: all three banking arms require house_card_shown, which is an accomplishment gate and therefore HIDES rather than locks. Walked BEFORE the card, so this is that player. ==

His shipped talk_pool bark still serves the FIRST interact (the additive-conversation contract, and stationer_room_loop's own pin, live here). talk_pool_line is counter-driven, not rng-driven (social.gd: chatted_with_<id> % pool.size()), so serving it here instead of later moves no other line in this run.
steps.name: interact

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: Contracts, letters, and the occasional apology. The apologies pay best and take longest.

steps._comment: THE GATE PIN, pinned WHOLE: TWO rows, not five. The [Charming Smile] arm, the 8-gold arm and the [Appraise Foe] arm are all gone -- hidden, not locked -- and what is left is his ungated refusal and the exit. A regression that drops the house_card_shown requirement puts three rows back into this array and fails here, before any counter can bank.

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: The blank seal is eight gold the hour and it goes back in the tray when the hour is up. That is the entire arrangement, sir, and I have never been asked a second question about it.

options.text: "Who has been hiring the blank seal?"

steps._comment: Out through the ungated exit, having banked nothing at all.
== THE CARD. setting_commissioned is banked, so her pool serves the stationer_client_setting_done STAGE, not the base pool. ==

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: I wear it to the difficult errands now. That was always what it was for.

steps._comment: THE HUB PIN. Last-match-wins puts her on the shipped setting_commissioned variant (none of the three v0.18 variants match yet), and the option array is EXACTLY the new entry row plus the shipped ungated exit -- the proof that adding five rows to this node moved nothing a shipped canonical renders.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: It sits differently on the chain. I noticed before I looked. You were paid for the silver. Thank you for the remainder.

options.text: "You've been holding that card since I came in."

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: It came to my rooms before breakfast. Cream, no crest on it, one line, in a hand I have seen twice in my life on paper I was not supposed to be holding either time. It asks me to confirm a signature.

steps._comment: THE FELT/SEEN LINE. Magnolia is named by nobody in this thread; this node is the whole of the house's presence in her voice.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: I have signed nothing of consequence since the year my mother died. I am not going to say whose hand it is in a shop with a scribe in it. You already know which house I mean, because I told you where this city is run from and you did not laugh at me. She does not write to people like me. She writes about them, and only once something with her attention on it has started to move.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: Somebody has, and it has been out in this city doing business without me for long enough that a woman who notices everything has seen it. I will not answer that card until I can say who. Start at the counter of this very shop. There is a scribe there who rents a blank seal by the hour and who has never once asked me how I am.

steps._comment: == THE CARRIAGE WAKE. Facade prop on the boulevard's blocked row 1, the boulevard_glazier idiom: bumped from the walkable row below. present_when armed by house_card_shown, so it did not exist ten steps ago. ==

payload_contains.text: Pink lacquer, gone before you turned your head. The boulevard takes a moment to remember it was doing something, and nobody on it says the name out loud.

steps._comment: == BEAT 1, THE SCRIBE, NOW THAT THE CARD HAS BEEN SHOWN. His pool was spent on the pre-quest leg above and social_talked only clears on sleep, so ONE interact opens the graph here -- the same shape the fight script pins on the beaten broker. ==

THE COUNTER PIN, and this script's own negative leg: five rows now -- the same node that served TWO before the card, with the three gated arms restored by house_card_shown -- with the [Appraise Foe] arm VISIBLE-LOCKED (fixture holds neither it nor [Stealth]) and the 8-gold arm SELECTABLE at 25 gold, carrying its price token from _priced_text because the spend rides the gate option itself.

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour

options.text: "Who has been hiring the blank seal?"
[Charming Smile] Ask about the handwriting instead of the name.
"I'll buy the hour you were not working." (8 gold)
[Appraise Foe] The blotter under his elbow.

steps._comment: THE FREE ASK IS A SIGNPOSTING LINE, NOT A SOLUTION (GH#50): row 0 is ungated, he refuses it, and it loops back to the counter having banked nothing.
steps.name: confirm

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: No. Coin doesn't change it. Neither does the manners, and I'll thank you for them anyway. The seal goes out and the hour goes in the book. Nothing else gets written down. No names. The day people stop believing that, I have not worked out what I do next.

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: The blank seal is eight gold the hour and it goes back in the tray when the hour is up. That is the entire arrangement, sir, and I have never been asked a second question about it.

steps._comment: Back on the counter with the same five rows and the cursor re-homed to row 0. Down 1 to the [Charming Smile] arm -- a TWO-NODE chain, so the Skill buys entry to the negotiation and not the answer (the GH#64 anti-auto-win shape).

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: Handwriting. Well. Handwriting I can talk about, I suppose. Go on and be charming. It is usually about paper.

payload_contains.speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
payload_contains.text: Then there is no confidence to keep. A confidence is a thing a client tells me, and this man was a renter who never said what he was renting. He works a table at the west end of the alleys, past the tea. He pays in coin and he pays late. That's all I know about him.

steps._comment: == BEAT 2, THE BROKER. His whole cluster is present_when/encounter_when armed by forged_hand_named, so it materialised on the beat that just banked. ==

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
payload_contains.text: Brass, boxwood, or wax. Boxwood is cheaper and it cracks, and the crack is always in the one letter you needed.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
payload_contains.text: Whatever it is, I can have it on paper by this evening, and nobody will ever prove I wrote it. Eleven years at this table. The Watch has my name, and my rates for that matter, since I have never hidden the rates. Nothing to pin to any of it, though they have come and looked.

steps._comment: THE THREE-PILLAR NODE, pinned whole. Row 0 is the 30-gold buy rendered LOCKED at 25 gold (the real-cost alternate, priced out of reach on this run); row 2 is [Stealth] LOCKED; row 1 is the persuade this route takes. One node, three pillars, and two of them visibly refused.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
payload_contains.text: I cut blocks. A block is brass. What a man presses it into is between him and whoever reads the letter. That house has had nothing behind it since before I was born. The initials sat unused all that while, so I cut a block and I have rented it out since. Nobody living had a better claim, that I could find.

options.text: "Name your price for the block." (30 gold)
[Charming Smile] Tell him what the card cost her.
[Stealth] Take it off the table while he is still explaining.

steps._comment: ui_dialogue_shown fires once per OPEN, on the table node; `named` is the second node, so hold frames here instead.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
payload_contains.text: A card. To her. Cream, was it, and one line on it? I remember the stock. I did wonder at the time how far the paper would travel. Then the next customer sat down and I had a cut to price.

payload_contains.speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
payload_contains.text: Then take the brass and take it now, before anybody thinks to ask me where it went. I have been careful for eleven years about which names I borrow and I have never once borrowed upward. Tell them the block was destroyed. Tell them a bad season did it.

steps._comment: FIX ROUND 1: the SOCIAL fork banks its OWN counter. No gold moved on this arm and none should -- the assert two lines below holds gold at 25 across the whole broker leg -- so banking the purchase counter here was the mislabel.

payload_contains.text: He puts the brass in your hand and keeps his own hand out a moment longer, as if the table might want it back.

steps._comment: == BEAT 3, THE STEWARD. An original unnamed archetype at the Rest, present_when armed by house_card_shown -- she has been sitting there since the card was shown. ==

payload_contains.speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
payload_contains.text: The hearth is good here. I have sat in worse rooms for longer and been told they were an honour.

steps._comment: Her seal_block_settled variant, and the report array: ONLY the HANDED-OVER arm is visible -- the bought, lifted and taken arms are accomplishment-gated and therefore HIDDEN, never locked, which is the gating split working as designed. This row is the player-facing half of the fix: a run that spent nothing is no longer offered the buyer's line as its only way to report.

payload_contains.speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
payload_contains.text: You are carrying something with corners in your coat. Take the chair. Nobody in this house looks at what a guest sets on the table.

options.text: "He handed it over himself. He wanted it called destroyed. It isn't."

steps._comment: The felt/seen rule under direct interrogation: down 1 and ask her outright who sent her. She does not answer, and the refusal is the characterisation.

payload_contains.speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
payload_contains.text: A house sent me. Which house is not mine to say, and you have been in this city long enough not to ask a servant twice. I take a card out and I bring an answer back, and between those two things I keep the carriage ready and I wait.

payload_contains.speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
payload_contains.text: Good. Then he was selling it, and nobody had to take it from him, and the lady kept enough of the name to be worth the theft. That will go back exactly as you said it and not one word further. She is paid for her trouble and you are paid for yours. My mistress does not do favours. She does accounts, and she settles them the same week.

steps._comment: THE JOURNAL LINE (FIX ROUND 1, the surface the mislabel actually reached). completed_quest_summary renders resolved_path's text into the Completed list, so this is where a rung banked by the wrong fork becomes a sentence the player reads about themselves. Whole-list pin, the chronicle_loop idiom -- a future fork that forgets its own rung falls back to a sibling's ending line and fails here.
steps.name: journal

steps._comment: The LAST row is the one under repair: the SOCIAL route now closes on its own sentence, and that sentence does not contain the word bought. Before FIX ROUND 1 this same run rendered "You bought the block off him outright." here on 25 gold unspent. The two Invrisil rows also read as one arc: she paid somebody to say a true thing for her, and then said one herself.

completed_quest_lines: The Door That Goes Elsewhere — You consulted Pisces about it.
A Setting for a Lady (Invrisil) — You said the true thing about the stone out loud so she would never have to, and the setting was made honest around it.
Something Beneath — You brought the tremor's answer back up to Zevara, and she wrote the warren down as closed.
The Name and the Habit (Invrisil) — He put the brass into your hand for nothing and asked you to call it destroyed. You did not call it destroyed, and that is the part of it he will remember.

steps._comment: Pan to the Completed list before the shot -- the page opens on Act/Leads/Quests and the recorded ending sits below the fold. The body pans by DRAG, not by the option cursor (journal.gd _on_body_gui_input), so this is the drag_journal_body idiom field_skills_loop uses.
== THE LADY'S CODA. Her arc's close, and the third of the three v0.18 text_variants. ==

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: I answered it in my own hand. Two lines and no apology in either of them. That is the first thing I have signed in eleven years that nobody had to be told about afterwards.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: She has not replied. She will not. That is not how any of it works and I would not have the first idea what to do with a reply if one came. What I have instead is a card in a drawer with my own name on the back of it. I have taken it out twice this morning already. I could not tell you why.

payload_contains.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
payload_contains.text: Three, then. Do not tell me the third one is the ring. I would have to be gracious about it and I have used all of that up this week.

steps._comment: Scope guards: this is the pure-talk route. No fight anywhere, and neither sibling route's counter is reachable from it.

THE FIX, stated negatively: this run never banks the PURCHASE counter. Restore the old effect on the broker's talk_close arm and this line fails, before the journal ever gets a chance to call it a purchase.
